# Yosoi Docs

Source files for the [Yosoi](https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi) documentation, served at [cascadinglabs.com/yosoi](https://cascadinglabs.com/yosoi).

## Structure

- **yosoi/** -Core docs: introduction, installation, quickstart, and configuration
- **guides/** -How-to guides covering selectors, multi-item extraction, concurrency, custom types, and more
- **reference/** -Auto-generated API reference (produced by `scripts/generate_api_docs.py` in the Yosoi repo)

## Contact

[contact@cascadinglabs.com](mailto:contact@cascadinglabs.com)

## License

Apache-2.0

---

# contributing.mdx

Source: https://github.com/cascadinglabs/yosoi-docs/blob/main/contributing.mdx

---
title: Contributing
description: How to contribute to Yosoi and who maintains the project.
slug: contributing
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Contributions are welcome. Below is what you need to get started.

## Setting Up

<Steps>
1. Install with dev dependencies

   ```bash
   uv sync --all-groups
   ```

2. Install the pre-commit hooks

   ```bash
   uvx prek install
   ```

3. Happy Coding!

</Steps>

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose | Command |
|------|---------|---------|
| **Ruff** | Linting & Formatting | `uv run ruff check .` |
| **Mypy** | Type Checking | `uv run mypy .` |
| **Pytest** | Testing | `uv run pytest` |
| **Prek** | Git Hooks | `uvx prek run --all-files` |

## Commit Guidelines

We prefer (don't require) [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```bash
git commit -m "feat: add new selector discovery feature"
git commit -m "fix: handle missing author tags"
git commit -m "docs: update README with examples"
```

**Commit types:** `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`

## Pull Request Guidelines

When opening a PR, please include:

1. **Intent** -- what the PR does and why.
2. **Changes** -- a summary of what was changed.
3. **GenAI usage** -- if you used AI to write any of the code, include the prompts you used.
4. **Risks** -- any risks or side effects this PR might introduce.
5. **Docs** -- if needed, there should be a related PR to the [docs repository](https://github.com/CascadingLabs/YosoiDocs)

# roadmap.mdx

Source: https://github.com/cascadinglabs/yosoi-docs/blob/main/roadmap.mdx

---
title: Roadmap
description: Planned features and future direction for Yosoi.
---

import { Card, Badge, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

If something isn't shipped yet, you'll find it in one of two places:

1. **Here** -- on this page, as a major planned item
2. **[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues)** -- as a tracked issue in the Yosoi repo

If you want to follow progress on a specific feature, the GitHub issue is the most granular source. If you want a high-level picture of where the project is headed, start here.

---

## Planned

<div class="roadmap-section">

<Card title="Proxy Support">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

First-class proxy configuration for routing requests through dedicated residential or datacenter providers. See the [Proxying](/guides/proxying/) page for ethical guidance and planned scope.

</Card>

<Card title="Scaling & Distributed Pipelines">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

Integrations with Redis<sup>[⬡](#ref-6)</sup>, RabbitMQ, Prefect, Langfuse, and Turso<sup>[◎](#ref-7)</sup> for running Yosoi across multiple machines with shared selector caches and job coordination. See the [Scaling](/guides/scaling/) page for the full integration roadmap.

</Card>

<Card title="QScrape L2 Sites">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

Fictional SPA test sites (React<sup>[○](#ref-2)</sup>, Vue<sup>[◑](#ref-3)</sup>, Svelte<sup>[◇](#ref-4)</sup>, Solid<sup>[★](#ref-5)</sup>) for benchmarking browser-backed fetching and DOM discovery against known, stable targets. Mirrors the existing L1 suite.

</Card>

<Card title="Distributed Selector Cache">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

Redis<sup>[⬡](#ref-6)</sup> and Turso<sup>[◎](#ref-7)</sup>-backed selector storage for teams sharing discovery results across machines and CI runs. See [Scaling](/guides/scaling/).

</Card>

<Card title="Versioned Docs">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

Per-release documentation snapshots so older API versions remain accessible.

</Card>

<Card title="Conda Forge Distribution">

<Badge text="Planned" variant="success" size="small" />

Publish Yosoi to Conda Forge to make installation as easy as possible for users in the conda ecosystem.

<LinkCard title="Issue #56" href="https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues/56" description="Track this feature on GitHub" />

</Card>

</div>

## Proposed

<div class="roadmap-section">

<Card title="DOM-Enabled Scraping (A3Nodes)">

<Badge text="Experimental" variant="caution" size="small" />

The first A3Node slice is shipped behind `experimental_a3node=True` and works with browser-backed fetching. The broader node-based DOM architecture remains active development: richer action graphs, replay health, and long-lived stability recipes are still evolving.

This introduces a new class of selector that can capture DOM assertions, actions, and arrangements (A3) without needing a bulky LLM to drive.

</Card>

<Card title="Canonicalization Engine">

<Badge text="Proposed" variant="note" size="small" />

A mode that merges selector caches across domains that serve the same content. If two sources (e.g. thewallstreetjournal.com and wsj.com) publish equivalent data, enabling canonicalization on a contract would collapse them into a single canonical selector set. Reducing redundant discovery and keeping extraction consistent. Implementation would likely involve tracing or logging logic to detect overlapping field mappings, then coercing the duplicate into the canonical domain's cache. May warrant a separate repo/package.

<LinkCard title="Issue #39" href="https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues/39" description="Track this feature on GitHub" />

</Card>

<Card title="Super Crawler">

<Badge text="Proposed" variant="note" size="small" />

A first-class multi-page crawling mode. Currently Yosoi operates on single pages -- there is no way to chain together multiple linked pages. Multi-page crawling is a common use-case that makes sense to include natively. This would likely require expanding the AI generation step so that stateful "steps" are defined for the LLM to replay its predecessor's selectors and JavaScript actions needed to complete a crawl. With DOM-enabled rendering progressing rapidly via the A3Nodes work above, this is becoming increasingly viable.

<LinkCard title="Issue #34" href="https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues/34" description="Track this feature on GitHub" />

</Card>

<Card title="Smart Batching of Tokens">

<Badge text="Proposed" variant="note" size="small" />

Currently the pipeline sends N requests (one per contract field), each containing the full HTML, and hopes the LLM's context window is large enough. This needs to be more defensive. A smart batching or context management system would use a lightweight lxml pre-processor to trim the HTML to a safe-enough, close-enough subset per contract -- reducing token cost and avoiding context window overflows.

<LinkCard title="Issue #50" href="https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues/50" description="Track this feature on GitHub" />

</Card>

<Card title="Dynamic Schema Builder">

<Badge text="Proposed" variant="note" size="small" />

A JSON codegen tool that lets users define a schema in JSON and generates a Pydantic contract from it. This lowers the barrier for newcomers who find OOP-style contract definitions (`ys.Contract`) intimidating but still need the specificity that Pydantic models provide for structured LLM output. Useful for REST and MCP design workflows as well. The `Prompt → Contract → Selectors → Content` pipeline would gain a new entry point.

<LinkCard title="Issue #33" href="https://github.com/CascadingLabs/Yosoi/issues/33" description="Track this feature on GitHub" />

</Card>

<Card title="Custom Yosoi SLMs">

<Badge text="Proposed" variant="note" size="small" />

Custom Small Language Model for fully offline private scraping ≤ 3 billion parameters.

</Card>

</div>

## References

<a id="ref-1"></a>△ **Zendriver**. cdpdriver. *Python-based browser automation using the Chrome DevTools Protocol.* https://github.com/cdpdriver/zendriver

<a id="ref-2"></a>○ **React**. Meta. *JavaScript library for building user interfaces.* https://react.dev/

<a id="ref-3"></a>◑ **Vue**. Evan You. *Progressive JavaScript framework for building UIs.* https://vuejs.org/

<a id="ref-4"></a>◇ **Svelte**. Rich Harris. *Compiler-based frontend framework.* https://svelte.dev/

<a id="ref-5"></a>★ **Solid**. Ryan Carniato. *Fine-grained reactive UI library with no virtual DOM.* https://www.solidjs.com/

<a id="ref-6"></a>⬡ **Redis**. Redis Ltd. *In-memory data structure store used as a database, cache, and message broker.* https://redis.io/docs/

<a id="ref-7"></a>◎ **Turso**. Turso. *Edge-hosted distributed SQLite database.* https://turso.tech/
